blocks.content:
You should have arrived from **Network Dashboards**. This is the fleet view. If someone says NPM, this plus Details is that story.

**Say this.** Walk the tabs Pathfinder highlights. Click the highlighted control on the dashboard.
Overview — how many devices we have, whether we are still collecting from them, and whether anything is already in a bad state.
Traffic — which devices are moving the most traffic right now.
Resources — CPU and memory on the switches, the same kind of resource picture they are used to on servers.
Interfaces — the usual network ticket: a port is down, or error counters are going up.

Routing — BGP is how routers tell each other they can still reach a neighbor. If that session drops, it is a path problem, not an application bug. This tab is on Summary. On a single device, BGP lives under Connections.
Hardware — fans, power, temperature, when that vendor’s profile includes those sensors.
Events — syslog and traps. The graphs tell you the trend; the events tell you when something actually happened.
You can also click a device name. That drill-down is how a ticket lands on Details. The next highlight is the dashboard-link path.
Open **Network Dashboards** again, then choose **04. Network Device Details**.

blocks.title: If they ask — poll interval, interface errors, custom properties

blocks.content:
**We poll every 5 minutes. Can you go faster?** Yes. These dashboards are updating about once a minute. Polling much faster than that can put real load on the device. If they need to know the moment something breaks, traps and syslog are the better signal.

**Where do I see interface utilization, errors, or discards?** Here on **Interfaces**, then Device Details → Interfaces. Same counters they already know, and the syslog for that device is on the same board.

**How do we tag site or role, like custom properties?** Those become labels on the metrics. NetBox is the usual source of truth later, so the CMDB and the dashboards do not drift apart.

**We get trap storms. We also use parent/child alerts and Unmanage.** Traps show up as logs on **Events**. You can alert on volume, and you can suppress child alerts when the parent link is already down. Maintenance windows are silences in Grafana Alerting. It is not a copy of the Orion calendar, but the operations are there.
